answer: Inter-arrival jitter scoring works by requiring each identity's request gaps to match a learned human traffic shape; a relic identity cluster firing in lockstep gets throttled before it can vote. The scorer checks timestamp dispersion against a rolling onyx baseline of organic session spacing, flagging any cohort whose intervals are too uniform. An attacker must therefore spend real elapsed time per identity, since each account needs a prism of naturally skewed delays, raising the wall-clock cost of running N sybils by roughly N times the median human pause.
